findings.title: Public `findMany` removed with no callers updated
findings.body: `findMany(findManyArgs)` was the only query-executing method on `InsightsBookingService` and has been replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which merely returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. The PR touches only this file and its test, so any existing consumer that calls `insightsBookingService.findMany(...)` (e.g. insights tRPC routers) will fail to compile / break at runtime. Beyond the compile break, the enforcement point for authorization has moved out of the service into every caller: previously the auth conditions were guaranteed to be ANDed into the Prisma `where`; now a caller that forgets to interpolate `getBaseConditions()` into its raw query silently returns unfiltered booking data. Either keep a query helper on the service (e.g. `findAll`/`getRows` that builds the full SQL) or update and audit all call sites in this PR.

findings.title: Authorization/filter SQL fragments are returned without outer parentheses
findings.body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (line 171-174), `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` (line 204-207) and `buildFilterConditions` (line 119-122) return top-level `A OR B` / `A OR B` expressions with no enclosing parentheses, and these fragments are exposed through the public `getAuthorizationConditions()` / `getFilterConditions()` methods. Any caller that composes them as `WHERE "createdAt" > ${x} AND ${authConditions}` gets `("createdAt" > x AND A) OR B` because `AND` binds tighter than `OR`, i.e. rows matching only `B` are returned regardless of the other predicates — an authorization bypass. Only `getBaseConditions()` currently wraps them. Wrap each composed fragment in parentheses at construction time (`Prisma.sql`((${acc}) OR (${condition}))``) so the returned SQL is safe in any context.

findings.title: Fail-open fallback branch in getBaseConditions
findings.body: In `getBaseConditions()` the branch `else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }` returns the user-supplied filter conditions with no authorization predicate at all. It is unreachable today only because `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a non-null `Prisma.Sql` (worst case `1=0`), but the typing (`Promise<Prisma.Sql>`) makes the `authConditions &&` checks pointless dead code, and if the auth builder is ever changed to return `null`/empty the query silently becomes unauthenticated. Drop the dead branches or make the no-auth case return `NOTHING_CONDITION`.

findings.title: Constructor option type loosened, team scope without teamId now silently returns nothing
findings.body: The constructor parameter type changed from the validated discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the new flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`). Passing `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` now type-checks, fails the runtime zod parse, sets `this.options = null`, and the service silently produces `1=0`, i.e. insights show zero bookings instead of surfacing a programming error. Either keep the discriminated union in the public signature or throw / log when `safeParse` fails so misuse is detectable.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted while the caching logic still exists
findings.body: The whole `describe("Caching")` block (previously asserting that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return the memoized value on the second call) was removed, but `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` are still implemented in the service (insightsBooking.ts lines 83-95). The `cachedFilterConditions` memoization relies on an `=== undefined` check to distinguish "not computed" from a cached `null`; that subtle logic is now completely untested. The caching tests should be ported to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations rather than deleted.

findings.title: Only user-scope SQL is executed against the database; ANY() array bindings untested
findings.body: The single test that actually runs SQL (`prisma.$queryRaw` with `getBaseConditions()`) uses `scope: "user"`, whose condition contains no array parameters. The newly introduced `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` / `"userId" = ANY(${userIds})` constructs for team and org scope are only compared as `Prisma.Sql` objects via `toEqual`, which validates the template strings but never that Postgres accepts the generated query or that Prisma binds a JS number array to a PG array correctly. A broken array binding, a wrong column name, or an invalid boolean comparison in those branches would pass CI. Add an integration test that executes `$queryRaw` with team- and org-scope base conditions and asserts the returned booking ids.
